scope: Theorem 4.3 (Prescribed widths for a locally finite family) of the manuscript “Positive scalar curvature and uniform codimension-two width” (preprints/Positive-scalar-curvature-and-uniform-codimension-two-width-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 336 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f67c30579306bd4d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 21. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let (M, g) be complete, connected and smooth, with Scalg ≥ 1. There is a countable set of centers (xi) such that Ai = Bg(xi, D), Bi = M \ Bg(xi, 2D) have the following properties: the Ai cover M, and the closed balls Bg(xi, 2D) are locally finite. Suppose that every Bi is nonempty. Given arbitrary finite numbers Li > 0, there exist a complete smooth metric h ≥ g and a countable family of smooth functions (pα), whose supports form a locally finite family of compact sets, for which disth(Ai, Bi) > Li (i ≥ 1), (4.6) Scalh −2∆h X α pα − d X α pα 2 h − X α |dpα|2 h ≥ 2 5 . (4.7) Every sum in (4.7) is locally finite. If some Bi is empty, then diamg M ≤ 4D.
